title: Preserve scope and authority across work-loop integration seams
summary: Unify work-loop projections through shared context and evidence, while keeping authority, delegation, clarification and learning promotion distinct. Validate caller scope before feedback effects and reject unsupported scope rather than silently widening it.
reusable_steps: Unify work-loop projections through shared context and evidence, while keeping authority, delegation, clarification and learning promotion distinct
Validate caller scope before feedback effects and reject unsupported scope rather than silently widening it
expected_outcome: Use the Organization Work Loop as the parent model and describe intent, enterprise, user interaction and memory as projections, not competing ledgers. Evaluate evidence, scope, explicit authority, risk, capability and verification at relevant transitions. Delegation and confidence do not confer permission. Validate the exact feedback context before any effect; retain the original execution correlation and never turn acknowledgement into unrelated execution. At CLI boundaries, pass supported scope explicitly and reject unsupported scope flags. Test mismatch and malformed-input paths as well as success. Report recorded feedback separately from promoted knowledge and actual next-work consumption. Document mission continuation and scoped learning as pending until durable claim/receipt, current-authority revalidation, unknown-outcome reconciliation and scoped consumption are implemented and verified. This lesson was manually curated from a structurally distilled bounded increment; no provider consistency assessment or live authenticated end-to-end success is claimed.
